newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia cotton marginally affected by rain.
newsitem.headline: Australia cotton marginally affected by rain.

text.p: Australia's A$1 billion cotton crop would be very marginally affected by rain from cyclone Justin which recently hit the state of Queensland, Peter Corish, chairman of peak industry body Cotton Australia Ltd, told Reuters.
Some rain had fallen in central Queensland in the Emerald district, he said.
"It will have some impact but there hasn't been any huge devastation. It will probably be just a little bit of downgrading," he said.
Corish said he could not quantify the effect, which would depend largely on the weather from now on. But it would be "relatively small, very very marginal", he said.
Australia's cotton crop was still headed for 2.4 to 2.5 million 500 pound bales, he said.

Harvesting had begun on some farms in the Goondiwindi area of Queensland, near the New South Wales border, a week ago, he said. The pick across the industry would be in full swing in about a fortnight, he said.
The Australian Cotton Foundation last week changed its name to Cotton Australia in a re-launch of the organisation.
